subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw natively carry framework-authenticated source, review, and influence metadata across its memory plugin contract, or leave trust-governed memory entirely to external plugins and MCP backends?
rationale: The choice defines OpenClaw's memory security boundary, persistent data model, plugin compatibility contract, and whether default memory-core must enforce policy; repository behavior and existing external implementations cannot establish that product intent automatically.

options.title: Add a generic trust contract
options.body: Extend the portable memory SDK and builtin backend with framework-assigned provenance, orthogonal review/influence state, migrations, and retrieval enforcement.

options.title: Keep trust plugin-owned
options.body: Document memory-core as operator-trusted storage and route trust-governed memory to external plugins or MCP backends such as world-model-mcp.

options.title: Limit scope to provenance
options.body: First land source attribution through the portable contract, while tracking expiration and influence enforcement as separately approved follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Add a generic trust contract
recommendation.body: Extend the portable memory SDK and builtin backend with framework-assigned provenance, orthogonal review/influence state, migrations, and retrieval enforcement.
